answer: Divergent-challenge registration. Each identity must solve a fresh random challenge whose seed includes a secret held only in memory; a clone net replaying answers stalls. On any challenge, an ember of the answer must match the node’s own prior signed history. Honest agents wander across challenge types freely, but copies cannot diverge without breaking signatures. Attackers must run one full instance per identity, and a shale of compute per clone makes N identities cost N times the work.
